findings.where: Article specimen, the pull quote “Whichever PPP Law I am currently working on with a client country!” (desktop-03, phone-02)
findings.fault: The quote is set in logo blue, the colour the tile's own palette gives to links and the button. Elsewhere on the page that blue means 'click this'. Here it marks static text. The real link in the same column, the lecture title, is also blue, so the two read as the same kind of thing.
findings.who_objects: A reader of an article tries the large blue line as a link and nothing happens. Angélique, adding posts later, can no longer tell from the look which blue text is a link. The palette tile's own role note ('wordmark, links, the button') is broken by its own specimen.

findings.where: Hero, the first screen's 'Get in touch' button, and the end of the page (no footer)
findings.fault: The only contact route is a button that opens a mailto. Mark's email address never appears as text anywhere on the page, and the page ends on 'Play again' with no footer or written address. The nav 'Contact' link goes to '#' and does nothing.
findings.who_objects: Development-bank staff on locked-down work machines or webmail click 'Get in touch', and either nothing opens or a mail client they don't use opens. They then find no address to copy. This is the one action the site exists for (brand sheet §1; first-visit trust item 7).

findings.where: Hero, the lead paragraph under the headline (desktop-01, phone-01)
findings.fault: The hero speaks about Mark in the third person ('Advice … from a former Lead Lawyer…'), like a firm's brochure. It closes on a size claim, 'Over 40 years of international infrastructure experience', not on checkable work. No line on the first screen is in Mark's own voice, though the brief's v5 take asks for 'his own words' in the headline.
findings.who_objects: Mark, who asked that the individual be the brand and that the firm voice go (§5, client values 1, 3 and 6). Procurement readers at development banks, who judge by named work and regions, not years counted (first-visit trust, 'Feel the CV').

findings.where: Style-tile section labels: 'Texture' and 'Motion sketch' against 'Palette', 'Type pair' and 'An article page' (desktop-02, phone-01, phone-02)
findings.fault: Labels of the same kind get two treatments. Two have a hairline rule under them and three have none, so the sections look as if they belong to different systems.
findings.who_objects: The layout-round designer reading this tile as the rulebook for headings and dividers can't tell which treatment is the house one.

findings.where: Motion sketch, the heading 'precise, light, quick' (desktop-02, phone-02)
findings.fault: It is set as a large display heading in Source Sans and in a lighter grey. The type-pair note directly above says Source Sans is for 'the nav, buttons, labels and dates only' and that Gelasio carries headings. The tile breaks its own type rule one section later.
findings.who_objects: The layout and animation rounds, which must draw inside this tile's rules and are shown two contradicting ones.

findings.where: Article specimen headline 'The World's Best…' and hero 'World Bank's'
findings.fault: The apostrophes render as straight typewriter marks. The same page's quotes are curly (“…”, ‘Abundance’), so the punctuation is mixed inside one serif voice.
findings.who_objects: A careful reader, a lawyer audience included, sees a typesetting slip in the largest type on the page. It undercuts the polished Georgia look the direction rests on.

findings.where: Article specimen, the byline line 'MMM Infra Blog No. 8 · 18 September 2024', and the nav's separate 'Articles' and 'Blog'
findings.fault: The article is credited to 'MMM Infra', not to Mark, though it is written as 'me'. The specimen is headed 'An article page' but labels itself a blog post, while the nav offers both 'Articles' and 'Blog'. A visitor can't tell which of the two holds this piece.
findings.who_objects: A visitor who lands on an article from a LinkedIn post and needs to see who wrote it (first-visit trust item 12). Mark, whose brand is himself, not the firm (§5).

findings.fault: A button that acts in place wears the link look: blue, underlined text. That treatment is reserved for links elsewhere on the page, as on the lecture title.
findings.who_objects: A visitor expects the underlined blue words to take them somewhere and gets an in-place replay. Small, but it teaches the wrong meaning for the underline.

findings.where: Header at phone width, the logo lockup (phone-01)
findings.fault: At phone width the lockup drops 'Moseley Infrastructure Advisory Services' and leaves the arches over 'MMM INFRA'. This shortened logo is not one the client holds, and on phones it hides who MMM Infra is.
findings.who_objects: Mark, whose brand sheet keeps the full mark with the long name to its right (§4, client value 7). A phone visitor arriving from LinkedIn sees only initials until the headline.
